event.summary: Archive epoch can change without waking other clients
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 06d4b68f3a9e913f47cd426fedee5946a4eed77b

## TLDR
After deleting a session that archives its checkout, other open windows can keep an empty or outdated Trash count until another fleet change or an explicit Trash open. A filtered window can miss the newly archived work entirely in its idle Trash display.

## Details
The new archive branch in crates/farhelm-helm/src/sessions.rs:3376-3382 increments trash_requests but relies on forget_deleted_session to publish the fleet wake; finish_replacement:4195-4202 has the same reliance. That tail calls manager.forget_session. At manager.rs:2405-2434, forgetting only bumps FleetEvents when it actually removed a cached/live session. The supervisor can legitimately make that removal observable before the delete reply: service/teardown.rs:1062-1065 removes the session and hints SessionsChanged, then :1081 onward performs unbounded on-disk cleanup, including discard_quarantined at :1149-1150. The request handler only sends SessionDeleted after that teardown returns (service/handlers.rs:1369-1382). The manager can therefore consume the hint, commit a list without the session, and bump the fleet (manager.rs:4603-4615,4659-4662) while the Trash epoch is still old. Another client's completed hosts read can consume that wake. Later the reply increments the epoch, but forgetting the already-removed row returns false (store.rs:9227-9237), so no new event is emitted. This is a source-established ordering, especially visible when post-removal attachment cleanup is slow; it does not require a forged request or unshipped control.

Other idle windows have no guaranteed repair timer: feed.rs:233-234 disables fallback polling with a healthy feed, list/view.rs:2314-2320 reads hosts on fleet notifications, and list/trash.rs:737-768 invalidates its reader only on the delivered epoch or other explicit causes. Stable periodic manager refreshes have no cache change or unanswered hint and need not emit another event (manager.rs:4659-4662). A window whose complete listing shows the removed managed row may independently refresh Trash; filtered/truncated windows are the explicit motivation of the new code and lack that fallback.

Contract: SPEC_impl.md:4538-4542 says `A per-host in-memory Trash epoch advances on accepted nonempty Delete or Retry, on a session Delete or Replace that archived a checkout, and on a recorded notice change, before the existing fleet wake. Hosts listings carry it; only its change invalidates an idle host’s Trash reader`. The archive fact is a separate observable change even when the session cache is already current. Publish an explicit fleet bump after advancing the epoch in both archive branches, rather than depending on a changed-only session-cache deletion.

Suggested bucket: high/material UX (other windows can retain an incorrect Trash count indefinitely during an otherwise idle healthy connection). Confidence: confirmed by source and contract analysis; no execution, build or reproduction. Could-be-highest: no; files remain archived and retrievable, and no security or data-loss route is claimed. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none; coverage/queue sources were not read. Caveats: an unrelated later event, reconnect, app load or explicit dialog opening repairs the display; the issuing window may already perform its own refresh. This does not claim that archived files are lost.

# Stopped actors delay the manager's direct-drop cleanup

Reviewed commit: 56659839785691f76da3af5d8f51b511cff4ba8b

## TLDR
Releasing a connection manager without explicitly shutting it down can leave its tasks and unrelated supervisor connections alive while a stopped environment actor waits. Overlapping idle actors may retain each other indefinitely; normal graceful helm shutdown explicitly cancels them and is outside this finding.

## Details
Revises local synthesis lead f3; independently inspected the exact source named by g024/l5 event35. manager.rs:3845 initializes a named Option<Arc<ConnectionManager>> by upgrading the actor's Weak reference. :3846-3855 borrows it to check the place. Its only move at :3864 belongs to a left-to-right short-circuited condition requiring !stopped.attempted and gate. When either is false, the local remains owned throughout the same arm's idle select loop at :3873-3892. A named owned local is dropped at the end of that arm, not at its last borrow; the wait can retain the last strong manager reference. The idle reference is unnecessary after gate calculation.

This prevents the documented direct-drop cleanup from being entered immediately: the manager owns its actor map and ConnectionManager::drop at :3137-3145 calls shutdown. shutdown/withdraw_actors at :3093-3133 withdraws published clients and aborts all actors. The module explicitly says actors hold only Weak so the manager/actor map can be dropped (:1161). Its direct-drop test at :11929-11975 actually drops the manager without explicit shutdown, expects connection closure and no further dials, but its fixture creates an ordinary SSH host rather than a Stopped environment. Fixture at :7425-7430 has no cleanup override. Thus the contract is source-visible even though normal serving uses a stronger explicit shutdown.

Independent graceful-caller checks: lib.rs:2574-2585 always reaches state.manager.shutdown_and_wait after its serving select, and rest_harness.rs:1007-1010 explicitly calls manager.shutdown before drop. This record does not claim an ordinary desktop/standalone graceful shutdown hang, process/work loss, or an unbounded leak from one stopped actor alone. The original conditional indefinite-retention consequence from g024/l5 is retained for source confirmation of the supported repeated-Stopped route and endpoint/attribution next; the already confirmed narrower consequence is delayed fallback manager/resource cleanup.

Suggested bucket: other, resource lifetime/API/fixture correctness. Confidence: confirmed source/language analysis for strong retention across the idle wait; not runtime observed. Could-be-highest:false, no security or user-work-loss route established. proposed_drop:false. possible_cover:g024/l5 event35 supplied by caller identifies the same mechanism; preserve both owners for parent consolidation. No tests, builds, runtime reproduction or live action. Fix direction: confine the place-gate upgrade to a short scope; separately upgrade/move only when an actual owned lifecycle start task needs it. Preserve that task's legitimate ownership and explicit shutdown.
